title: Niryasa 6. Acharya Prabhu's Vow; the Eight Kavirajas and Six Chakravartis
html:
Nine jewel-verses on Srinivasa's mission; in payar: the news of Mahaprabhu's departure, the dream and the order to go to Vrindavana; the news of the departure of Rupa and Sanatana and their appearance in a dream; initiation from Gopala Bhatta; Govinda's command; Srinivasa's padas on Govinda and on Guna Manjari; the gifts of Mahaprabhu and Raghunatha; departure for Gauda; the author's prayers; the colophon (Shaka 1529) and the list of Kavirajas and Chakravartis

1Nine verses: "Here Bhagavan, producing the pure truth of the Satvatas, revealed it through one of His shaktis named Sri Rupa; through another of His shaktis, manifesting in a pure brahmana family the one named Sri Srinivasa, Sri Prabhu Himself wound up His lila in Nilachala. (1) Sri Srinivasa Prabhu, who had resolved to go to Sri Purushottama, hearing from people's lips of the departure of Chaitanya, the ocean of mercy, fainted again and again from floods of grief; then merciful Bhagavan, seeing the devotee's pain, gave him in a dream this most wondrous command: (2) 'You have been born by Me as My own shakti; go quickly to Sri Vrindavana: there are the blessed Sri Rupa, Jiva and the others; I have already ordered them to entrust to you the jewels of their books; accept them without doubt and teach the people in Gauda.' (3) Receiving this command and turning his whole heart to it, Sri Srinivasa again set his mind on seeing the beauty of the groves of Sri Vrindavana; but hearing there of the departure of the Gosvamis, crying 'Alas, alas!' in grief, his heart distraught, he fell unconscious in the middle of the road. (4) In a dream Sri Rupa and the others, together with Srila Sanatana, said to him: 'This is no time for you to grieve, for Gopala Bhatta is there; therefore accept (from him) the best mantra and all the books composed by us, go to the land of Gauda, spread our teaching and instruct the Vaishnavas.' (5) His mind flooded with the nectar of that command, he entered Vrindavana and with devotion received from Gopala Bhatta Prabhu the whole truth of the mantra; expert in understanding service to him, sent by that glorious one with abundant prema to go to Gauda, he eagerly replied: (6) 'If by your grace those connected with me will attain the lotus feet of Radha and Krishna, then I shall go; otherwise why should I go?' Hearing all this, the best of the Gosvamis in great joy went with it to Govinda. (7) (Govinda said:) 'The command of those whose souls are wholly absorbed in meditation on Sri Govinda's lotus feet will bear fruit through shelter in Sri Srinivasa: in order to give (these books) he has been brought by Me to earth. Therefore let him go to Gauda; why this worry of yours here?' (8) Having drunk this nectar of command issuing from the moon-like lips of Sri Govinda, bowing to the assembly of Gosvamis with a glad heart and circumambulating them, taking with devotion the collection of books and setting out eagerly for the land of Gauda — may Sri Srinivasa Prabhu, the sole treasury of compassion, be ever victorious! (9)"1

2To reveal the pure lila of Vraja in Gauda,
(the Lord), as His heart desired, empowered Sri Rupa.

3Manifesting one shakti, empowering Sri Rupa,
He revealed the books with great joy.

4To reveal in Gauda what was in His heart,
Gaura had in His heart the desire to distribute it.

5Most wondrous was the shakti Gaura manifested —
who can understand the mind of Chaitanya?

6In Nilachala Mahaprabhu's manifest pastimes were going on;
the desire arose in (Srinivasa's) heart to see His holy feet.

7Leaving everything, Prabhu (Srinivasa) set out,
fixing his mind on the shelter of the holy feet.

8With desire in his heart he went on and on —
and on the way he received the news that Prabhu had disappeared.

9As soon as he heard it, he fell unconscious to the ground;
who can describe that ocean of grief?

10Again and again Prabhu (Srinivasa) faints, now unconscious,
now wailing and weeping.

11Then Mahaprabhu, seeing the devotee's grief,
came before him and began to speak:

12He comforted him much, placing His foot on his head,
and began to speak sweetly:

13"You are My own shakti, listen:
give up grief and go quickly to Vrindavana.

14Where Sri Rupa and Sanatana live,
there they have expanded the books on the pastimes of Radha and Krishna.

15Taking all those books, reveal them in Gauda
and distribute them with joy in your heart."

16Receiving the command, the nectar of His words,
he set out, bowing to Mahaprabhu's feet.

17Then he went to Sri Vrindavana:
"I shall see the beauty of its groves with my own eyes."

18Coming to Sri Mathura-mandala, he halted
and there heard that the two brothers had disappeared.

19As soon as he heard it, Prabhu fell, striking the ground,
and with cries lamented greatly:

20"If I have not been able to see the two brothers,
what further purpose is there in life?"

21Firmly resolving thus in his heart,
he fell unconscious at the foot of a tree.

22Then the two brothers, seeing the devotee's grief,
came, greatly pleased, to appear to him.

23Placing their feet on his head, they say to Prabhu:
"Look at us, look your fill."

24Seeing with his own eyes the beauty of Sri Rupa and Sanatana,
he felt a bliss that cannot be told.

25The two brothers, rejoicing, say:
"Through you the lowly, the wretched and the wicked will be delivered.

26Give up grief and go quickly;
take shelter at the feet of Sri Bhatta Gosani.

27From him you will receive initiation into the mantra;
through that is our mercy — what more can we say?

28With the mass of books you will go to Gauda
and deliver the living beings smitten by Kali."

29Receiving the command, these nectarean words,
he went to Vrindavana as revealed.

30Coming there, he saw the feet of Srila Gosvami,2
fell to the ground and offered many praises:

31"Be merciful to me, Prabhu, filled with compassion;
bring me to the goal, Prabhu, out of mercy."

32He told Prabhu the whole command of the two brothers,
and the Gosani understood why he had come.

33Hearing this, the Gosvami was boundlessly glad:
gooseflesh rose all over his body, tears flowed from his eyes.

34"Listen, Srinivasa, you are my life:
to see you I have held on to life.

35You are the life of my life;
for you Mahaprabhu gave this treasure.

36Look here: a letter written by Mahaprabhu's holy hand —
I have kept it carefully for you.3

37Look your fill at Prabhu's handwriting:
your good fortune, my son, is beyond words.

38And look further: the seat on which Mahaprabhu sat,
and the cord — He carefully sent them to me.

39Sitting on this seat given by Mahaprabhu,
I shall give you initiation into the mantra in great bliss."

40Sitting on the seat, he gave him initiation into the mantra,
and then, giving him the collection of books, taught him.

41When my Prabhu had become expert in the books,
seeing this, all the Gosanis were pleased.

42They ordered: "Go to Gauda —
this is the order of Sri Rupa, there is no doubt."

43Sri Jiva says: "Listen, Acharya Mahashaya:
know for certain — this is Mahaprabhu's order.

44Once, for your sake, Mahaprabhu
sent a letter from Nilachala."

45Seeing the letter, my Prabhu began to weep
and, weeping and weeping, fell into thought.

46("He who is born as the embodiment of prema, named Srinivasa —
I am not to see him: the Creator has left Me without hope.")4

47(So) the Gosani mercifully told me;
(and further:) "Having entrusted all the books to Srinivasa, (say to him):

48'Take these books and go to Gauda';
this is Mahaprabhu's order — accept the collection of books."

49Then my Prabhu began to speak:
"In my heart was the desire always to remain with Prabhu,5

50to live in Vrindavana and serve Prabhu;
how, leaving this, shall I go to Gauda?

51But the guru's order is stronger — it cannot be otherwise."
And he made known the desire of his heart:

52"If I am indeed to go to Gauda,
then gladly give me this order:

53whoever, Prabhu, accepts a connection with me
will attain the feet of Radha and Krishna.

54Give this order all together, out of mercy;
otherwise I shall not go — listen attentively."

55Hearing this, all the Gosanis were boundlessly glad,
streams of prema flowed unceasingly from their eyes.

56All the Gosanis together, coming to Govinda,
entreated Him with joined palms:

57Sri Bhatta Gosani and Sri Dasa Raghunatha,
Sri Jiva Gosani and Raghunatha Bhatta,

58Lokanatha Gosani and Bhugarbha Thakura —
all prayed much to Sri Govinda,

59meditating in their hearts on Sri Govinda's two feet:
"Out of mercy give Srinivasa this order:

60whoever, Prabhu, accepts a connection with him
will attain the feet of Radha and Krishna."

61All gladly made this request;
hearing it, Sri Govinda gave the command:6

62"To taste rasa I descended in Gauda
and tasted rasa in many ways.

63Know the reason for which I descended:
I flooded all people, giving them the treasure of prema.

64By My shakti his birth has been manifested:
he was born as the embodiment of prema, and his name is Srinivasa.

65Whoever accepts in his heart a connection with him
will attain the feet of Radha and Krishna."

66Receiving the nectar of command from the moon-like lips of Sri Govinda,
all together heard it with straining ears:

67"Send him quickly to Gauda:
let him go, taking the collection of books."

68Then my Prabhu, circumambulating all,
fell to the ground and wept much, crying aloud.

69In everyone's heart the ocean of bliss swelled:
who can describe the bliss that came upon them?

70My Prabhu, having received the nectar of Sri Govinda's command,
described, gazing at Sri Govinda's moon-like face:

71This is the pada, in raga Suhai:
With what chisel was this moon-face carved, friend, who carved those two eyes?
As I look, my heart feels so strange — my very heart is witness to it. (1)
Who, friend, carefully cut the jewel and set it in (His) ear?
Together with my mind, my five life-breaths — I have become a yogini, meditating on Him. (2)
Above the nose shines the gajamukta pearl, set in gold on either side:
who is this — a crescent moon with lightning, smiling from behind a cloud? (3)
On the lovely forehead shines — what a lovely tilaka, friend! — and over it a row of curls;
deep in my heart it sparkles, friend — like a row of bees on the moon. (4)
That noose of Cupid — the tilt of His crown-chuda, friend — where did He learn it?
I have not seen it to my heart's content, friend — that is the great pain of my heart. (5)
With what sweet rasa His words are filled, friend — if only one could take them in one's hand!
If the Creator had made them so, friend, I would break off piece after piece and eat them. (6)
His arms are like the trunks of the best of elephants, friend, the curve of His arms, and at their tips red hingul;
the bird of youth, friend, dies of thirst, begging for the rasa of His touch. (7)
Who, as if anointing with nectar, adorned His forehead with a sandal tilaka?
Gazing at the moon-face, how can I hold my heart, how can my soul live? (8)
The tinkling of the anklets on His feet surpasses the khanjana bird's chirping, friend; His gait is slow as a rutting elephant's.
In the flood of nectarean rasa Srinivasa has drowned, friend: the Creator has fashioned an ocean of prema. (9)7

72Having relished this, all wept with their arms round each other's necks;
who can describe the bliss that came upon them?

73My Prabhu greeted all as befitted:
he bowed down like a rod, overflowing with prema.

74Some he embraced, to others he bowed;
mercy came upon all, according to their worth.

75Then the adhikari Gosvami Sri Krishna Pandita8
joyfully laid Govinda to rest;

76he brought Govinda's garland of command
and joyfully placed it round Prabhu's neck.

77Receiving the prasada garland, everyone rejoiced
and freely partook of prasada.

78Betel and tulasi garlands were given to all,
and then all returned to their lodgings.

79Another day, when all had gathered together,
they gave my Prabhu a command:

80"Listen, Srinivasa, go to Gauda,
carefully take the collection of books."

81Bhatta Gosani says: "Hear my word,
all of you together hear how Prabhu acted."

82Saying this, the Gosvami, with joy in his heart,
brought Gaura's kaupina and outer cloth

83and bound them on my Prabhu's head:
"When Prabhu was going to the South, He gave me a command:

84'My prasada cloth — the kaupina and outer cloth —
give to Srinivasa,' He ordered with great joy.

85And there was another command — hear it quickly:
'By your mercy let him know My mercy.'

86All this I told to the two (brothers):
I told it to Sri Rupa and Sanatana.

87Then the two brothers, hearing this,
were filled with prema — what happiness arose in them!"

88Hearing this, all the Gosanis rejoiced
and gave him leave to go to Gauda.

89Hearing this, my Prabhu, (addressing) Bhatta Gosvami,
describes the form of Sri Guna Manjari:

90Here is the pada:
Cluster of prema, listen, Guna Manjari: you alone are the giver of all good.
Unceasingly I meditate on your virtues — my mind is sold to you.
Hari, Hari! When will my auspicious day come?
The treasure of meeting the feet of Kishori and Kishora — shall I meet it together with you?
Seeing one in distress, cast your merciful glance, by your goodness fulfil my hope.
Without you, the new cloud, how will the chataka bird quench its thirst, begging for a drop of rain?
You alone are my refuge, certainly, certainly — such is the evidence in my heart.
Sorrowfully Srinivasa cries again and again: mercifully attend! (1)
You are Guna Manjari, foremost in beauty and virtue, the abode of sweet loveliness;
of all the young maidens of Vraja (you are) unceasing in loving service, and your radiant body is dark.
What can I say of your fame — (the Divine Couple) is subject to you in rasa; this my heart surely knows.
Making me your follower, casting a merciful glance, grant me the treasure of service.
I, a dwarf, wish to seize the moon — such is the desire of my heart;
this person is most wretched, you alone are the refuge: by your goodness fulfil my hope.
Joining my palms above my head, with a straw between my teeth, I pray again and again:
named Srinivasa Dasa, he begs for loving service in Vraja — in your retinue. (2)9

91When Prabhu composed this pada,
all rejoiced greatly at heart.

92Hearing the pada, all were filled with great joy;
Sri Dasa Gosvami was greatly pleased.

93Crying "Well done, well done!", he embraced Prabhu
and drenched his whole body with tears:

94"Listen, listen, Srinivasa — I say with great joy:
by the order of the two brothers — to see you —

95I, who never leave Sri Kunda even for a moment,
have come here to see you.

96As I heard of you, so I have seen you with my own eyes:
who can tell the limit of your good fortune?

97In separation from Sri Rupa my body is wasted,
in separation from Sanatana my heart burns.

98In separation from the two brothers I cannot hold on to life;
seeing you, I am comforted by the sweetness of your virtues.

99The happiness I had in the sight of the two of them,
that happiness will be found in meeting you.

100Look here: the stone of Govardhana given by Prabhu" —
and he let him touch the stone and the gunja garland.10

101"For you — a letter written by Mahaprabhu's hand:
we all listened to it carefully.

102For you — the nectar of Govinda's command,
for you the two brothers themselves spoke,

103for you all these books have been revealed;
to see you was everyone's hope.

104Whoever becomes a vessel of Bhatta Gosvami's mercy
will easily obtain all this treasure."

105Sri Bhatta Gosvami together with Sri Dasa Gosvami,
in waves of bliss, could not contain themselves.

106The kaupina, cloth and outer cloth given by Mahaprabhu
he bound on his head with great joy,

107put Govinda's prasada garland round his neck
and at that time gave him Vamshivadana and the shalagrama.11

108All bless him with joy in their hearts:
"May Sri Radha and Govinda fulfil your desires!

109May Rupa and Sanatana fulfil your desires!
Without delay go quickly to Gauda."

110Then Prabhu, bowing to the feet of his own Prabhu,
bowed to all, filled with joy.

111Taking everyone's leave on his head,
he bowed to each of the residents of Vraja.

112With joy in his heart, taking the collection of books,
he set his mind on going quickly to Gauda.

113All the Gosanis came to see him off,
and all the residents of Vraja went with them.

114When, seeing him off, they had gone one krosha,
longing came upon them all:

115"Alas, alas, Creator, what have you done!
Having given the treasure, why do you take it away again?

116Who can describe that separation?"
The animals, the birds and all wept.

117Turning pale, (the Gosvamis) grew a little calmer,
and all softly say to Prabhu:

118"Listen, listen, Srinivasa, we tell you:
reach Gauda safely, without obstacles."

119He (Srinivasa) set out for Gauda, the Gosvamis for Vrindavana;
along the way they all walked and wept.

120How he went to Gauda
is described in detail in the book Prema-vilasa:

121it was written at the command of Jahnava
and revealed by Nityananda Dasa.

122In it all these events are set out at length —
waves of words surpassing nectar.12

123With the books my Prabhu came to Gauda
and there showed you special mercy.

124The vow with which my Prabhu came —
I saw with my own eyes how he fulfilled it.

125The vow Prabhu took — this (king) is its witness:
I see in you the fulfilment of Prabhu's vow.

126You, brother, when you composed the two padas,
pointed to this in them:

127in the two padas two accounts are revealed —
what a wondrous extract of nectar!

128Here is the pada: Radha's feet are a mass of nectar: He made me a maidservant at those feet, He bound my heart to Gora's feet. Together with Sri Radha-ramana He showed me the bower-house, He revealed to me the love of the Two. For my offences He revealed to me His own dealings — what can I say of Your ways and judgement! When I sit, He comes and makes me rise, leads me to the bank of the Yamuna. What to do, what not to do — I am always pining to death, not for a moment can I be still."13

129"These words about you you yourself, brother, have spoken;
who can describe your good fortune?

130My Prabhu has given you initiation;
what further instruction should I give you?

131So I have told you, brother — what more to add?
Without fail serve Prabhu's feet — that is the essence.

132By his mercy this lot has fallen to you;
in your company I have found great happiness."

133Briefly I have told of the instruction to this king;
who could write down its endlessness and boundlessness?

134Staying in private, he instructed the king:
staying a month with the king, he told him everything.

135Having been instructed, the king gave the Kaviraja a village
and fell to the ground like a rod, rolling on it.

136With Ramachandra the king found bliss
and always remained at ease in the rasa of talk about Krishna.

137Thus I have told of the glories of Sri Acharya;
fortunate is he who hears this.

138Whoever hears this account with a pure heart —
the dust of his feet is the ornament of my head.

139To the feet of Sri Ramachandra my millions of obeisances,
from whose lips the king heard the essence of siddhanta.

140O merciful Prabhu, lord of Ramachandra,
out of mercy, Prabhu, bring me to the goal!

141O Sri Acharya Thakura, be merciful together with your associates:
birth after birth may I be a dog that eats your remnants.

142Being a dog, I shall live in that place;
perhaps some day you will show mercy with the corner of your eye.

143Be merciful, Prabhu, with a merciful heart:
birth after birth may I remain in your retinue.

144Hearing of your vow, my heart rejoices;
by your goodness be merciful and fulfil my hope.

145Be merciful, Prabhu, ocean of compassion:
for the deliverance of sinners you are the friend of the wretched.

146With a straw between my teeth I ask only one thing:
birth after birth may I sing in your retinue.

147What more can I say at your feet, Prabhu?
Accept this low one, (otherwise) unapproachable.

148For the deliverance of sinners you descended;
therefore, Prabhu, deliver such a wrongdoer as I.

149How much shall I, worthless and dull-witted, plead?
Understand yourself in your heart whatever pleases you.

150Whether you punish or show favour —
in the world there is no one but you; see and understand this.

151Be merciful, Prabhu, I take shelter;
out of mercy fulfil my desire.

152Apart from you, Prabhu, I have no other refuge;
be merciful now to the wretched and low.

153If by fate I have another birth,
may I there too meet your retinue.

154By great fortune being born in your retinue,
fulfil my hope, Prabhu, out of mercy.

155Then my mind's desire will be fulfilled, Prabhu:
birth after birth may I be the servant of the servant of your servants.

156Seeing my bad nature, restrain your heart;
and yet my heart trembles at your virtues.

157How many sinners you delivered by the breeze of compassion —
only the extreme sinner has remained in the land.

158Deliver such a person and show your power:
then the name "Deliverer of Sinners" will be justified.

159Even if you reject me in anger,
still, alas, longing for your virtues arises.

160Of the goal and the means I know nothing;
I know only one thing — that I am a servant through connection with you.

161Out of mercy fulfil the bonds of hope —
this is the request of this wretched and miserable one.

162Vaishnava Gosanis, my purifiers of the fallen,
out of mercy give me shelter at your feet, Prabhu.

163The hearts of you all do not see faults;
therefore…

164…do not count any fault against me.
I do not know my own good — whether it is good or bad;

165and yet I describe the virtues of Prabhu,
not knowing especially whether the description is good or bad.

166What I write is by the command of my Prabhu;14
leaving aside the faults, Prabhu, listen to it.

167With a straw between my teeth I make this request:
living at Budhuipara near Srimati,

168always floating in bliss on the bank of the Jahnavi —
in the year fifteen hundred and twenty-nine,

169in the month of Vaishakha, on the day of the full moon,
placing on my head the lotus feet of my Prabhu,

170I completed the book — listen attentively.15
The servant of the servant of the servants of Sri Krishna Chaitanya Prabhu,

171the servant of his servants — this Yadunandana Dasa.
Hearing the book, the Thakurani rejoiced at heart;

172from her holy lips the book received the name Karnananda.16
Srimati with her own people relished the book —

173her body thrilled, her eyes full of tears.
Then Srimati, placing her foot on my head,

174began to speak, smiling:
"You have satisfied my ears by letting me hear this book:

175at its touch on my hearing my heart is soothed.
Listen, listen, son, I tell you:

176it will give me great joy to hear this —
the company of Kavirajas and the company of Chakravartis:

177set them out in order and let me hear."
Then I, bowing to Prabhu's feet,17

178fell to the ground and praised her much at her feet;
taking Prabhu's command on my head, with joy in my heart

179I write, carrying out Prabhu's command:
the eight Kavirajas and the six Chakravartis —

180everyone in the world knows of this.
First I shall describe the eight Kavirajas,

181then I shall tell of the company of other Kavirajas.
1. The eldest of the Kavirajas is Ramachandra Kaviraja,

182manifest in the midst of the world.
2. His younger brother is Sri Kaviraja Govinda,

183seeing whose life the world rejoices.
3. Then Sri Karnapura Kaviraja Thakura,

184who abundantly described Prabhu's virtues.
4. Then I shall tell of Sri Nrisimha Kaviraja Thakura,

185whose bhajana is strong and whose nature is sweet.
5. Bhagavan Kaviraja, of sweet disposition,

186knows nothing but Prabhu's feet.
6. Vallavi Dasa Kaviraja, most pure in heart,

187has no other concern but the service of Prabhu's feet.
7. Then Sri Gopiramana Kaviraja Thakura,

188most blissful, full of virtues.
8. Then I shall tell of Kaviraja Sri Gokulananda,

189who unceasingly (honours) Prabhu's two feet.
The eight Kavirajas I have described;

190I shall tell of the others — listen.
9. The son of Sri Govinda, Kaviraja Divyasimha,

191an intoxicated bee at Prabhu's lotus feet.
10. Sri Vasudeva Kaviraja,18 11. Sri Vrindavana Dasa,

192who has great jubilation in the service of the Vaishnavas.
12. And I shall tell of Kaviraja Dasa Vanamali,

193most eager in service in the mind.
13. The most blissful Kaviraja Durgadasa,

194firm in faith in the remnants of the Vaishnavas' food.
14. A most fine connoisseur of rasa is Rupa Kaviraja Thakura,

195from whose eyes tears always flow, full of prema.
15. His brother is Sri Nimai Kaviraja,

196who has no other concern but the service of Prabhu's feet.
16. Shyamadasa Kaviraja is his half-brother,

197beautiful in form, a vessel of great wisdom.
17. Sri Narayana Kaviraja is Nrisimha's brother:

198what can I say of his virtues — they are beyond words.
18–19. The two brothers of Sri Vallavi Kaviraja,

199most eager in faith in Prabhu's feet:
the elder is Sri Ramadasa Kaviraja Thakura,

200devoted to Hari-nama, always full of Krishna-prema;
his younger brother is Kaviraja Gopala Dasa,

201firm in faith in the service of the Vaishnavas.
I have described nineteen Kavirajas,

202by merely remembering whom prema is awakened.
Now I shall tell — listen — of the company of Chakravartis:

203first hear of the six chief ones.
1. The best of the Chakravartis is the one named Sri Govinda:

204what can I say of him — everything in him is incomparable;
he serves Prabhu with body, mind and words,

205and apart from Prabhu's feet knows neither goddess nor god.
2–3. I shall tell of Prabhu's two brothers-in-law, listen:

206both are most expert and skilled in bhajana.
The elder is Sri Shyamadasa Chakravarti Thakura,

207most renowned, rich in rasa;
the younger is Ramachandra Chakravarti Thakura,

208seeing whose bhajana Prabhu was pleased.
4. Then I shall tell — listen — of Vyasa Chakravarti,

209who always lives in bliss in Vishnupura.
5. And I shall tell of Chakravarti Ramakrishna Thakura,

210always blissful, of sweet disposition.
6. Then I shall tell of Chakravarti Sri Gokulananda,

211who abides freely in the service of the Vaishnavas.
You have heard of the six Chakravartis;

212I shall tell of the others — listen attentively.
7. Maharaja Chakravarti Sri Vira Hambira,

213a great and steadfast devotee, faithful to Prabhu's feet.
8. The greatly virtuous Srila Dasa Chakravarti,

214on whose tongue Hari-nama always shines.
9. And the devotee Ramajaya Chakravarti Mahashaya,

215whose endless virtues cannot be told.
10. And the devotee Chakravarti Sri Radhavallabha,

216devoted to the name, rare in the world.
11. And the devotee Srila Rupa Ghataka Chakravarti,

217in whom the rasa of the pastimes of Radha and Krishna always shines.
12. And the devotee Chakravarti…

218…Thakura (of the line) of Thakuras,19
firmly attached to Prabhu's feet, full of virtues.

219Thus I have made known twelve Chakravartis,
by remembering whose names prema rejoices.

220Bowing to the feet of all these bhagavatas,
Prabhu20 heard this in supreme bliss.

221Hearing it, Srimati rejoiced at heart:
"Truly, this is my book — the Karnananda."

222Taking Srimati's command on my head,
in supreme bliss I wrote the Karnananda into a book.

223This narrative of the Karnananda is an extract of nectar:
at its touch on the ear, the joy of prema is born in the devotees.

224The daughter of Sri Acharya Prabhu is Srila Hemalata:
has not the Creator fashioned a wish-fulfilling creeper of prema?

225Her two lotus feet sport in my heart;
Yadunandana Dasa tells the account of the Karnananda.

Thus ends the sixth niryasa of the Sri Karnananda, called "Acharya Prabhu's Vow and the List of Names of the Eight Kavirajas and Six Chakravartis headed by Sri Ramachandra".

Notes

  1. The nine Sanskrit verses (the "necklace of nine jewels", 5.184) were apparently composed by the author himself or taken from a Sanskrit biography; the text in the edition is corrupt in places (especially vv. 7–8), translated by sense. The editor glosses v. 8: "as the giver of these books, this Srinivasa has been brought to earth".
  2. Gopala Bhatta Gosvami.
  3. The mention of a letter in Mahaprabhu's own hand is peculiar to the Karnananda; in the Prema-vilasa and the Bhakti-ratnakara the Lord sends Gopala Bhatta His seat and cord (cf. 5.137–140).
  4. Probably words from Mahaprabhu's letter (36) which Srinivasa recalls or reads; the change of speaker is not marked in the original.
  5. Here "Prabhu" is Srinivasa's guru, Gopala Bhatta.
  6. Govinda is the Deity Govindadeva in Vrindavana; His command is given as the speech of Krishna Himself, who descended in Gauda as Mahaprabhu (62–63).
  7. A pada of Srinivasa (signed "Srinivasa" in the 9th stanza) describing the form of Govindadeva in the mood of a gopi. The portrayal of the gopis' feelings is transcendental prema, not mundane passion (cf. the note to 1.318).
  8. Krishna Pandita, the servant (adhikari) of Govindadeva (cf. the Prema-vilasa glossary).
  9. A pada of Srinivasa addressed to Guna Manjari, the spiritual form of his guru Gopala Bhatta; signed "Srinivasa Dasa". "Cluster of prema" is an uncertain reading of the corrupt premaka-punjari. "A dwarf seizing the moon" is an image of boundless desire.
  10. The stone from Govardhana and the garland of gunja seeds given by Mahaprabhu to Raghunatha Dasa (CC Antya 6.288–300).
  11. Vamshivadana is the Deity served by Srinivasa (cf. 3.26).
  12. A direct reference to the Prema-vilasa of Nityananda Dasa, written at Jahnava's command, as to an existing book. Since the Karnananda is dated by its colophon to 1607, while the Prema-vilasa (in its present form) is late, the reference is one of the grounds for considering the text of the Karnananda to have been edited later (or, conversely, it testifies to an early core of the Prema-vilasa).
  13. Lines from Vira Hambira's two padas (1.317–318) brought together: Ramachandra shows that in them the king himself described Srinivasa's mercy. The edition gives them as one pada; the lines are apparently abridged.
  14. Here and below "my Prabhu", "Srimati", "the Thakurani" is Hemalata, the author's guru.
  15. The dating colophon: 1529 (Shaka era — 1607 CE), Vaishakha, full moon, at Budhuipara on the bank of the Ganga (Jahnavi). This date is the main basis of the traditional dating of the Karnananda; it agrees poorly with the events described (e.g. Srinivasa's grown grandsons and their disciples in niryasa 2, the reference to the Prema-vilasa in 6.120–122), so the text is considered to have been expanded later, and the date itself doubtful.
  16. Karnananda: "Joy for the Ears".
  17. That is, to Hemalata.
  18. Number 10 is missing in the edition; the numbering is restored in order.
  19. The name of the twelfth Chakravarti at the top of p. 122 of the edition has not survived (thakurer thakur, "Thakura of Thakuras" — perhaps an epithet). Below the line the editor gives the Sanskrit verses "Srinivasa-shakha" (from the 18th vilasa of the Prema-vilasa, as he notes): they are not part of the poem and are not translated; cf. the translation of these verses in our Prema-vilasa.
  20. Hemalata.
